q: Harness choice induces up to a 40× difference in tokens per solved task
r: Include: controlled comparison of harnesses with model held fixed, with token-cost and failure metrics, is an evaluation-method contribution (EC6 ii) on tasks including fresh implementation.

q: agents implement a REST API server and modify it across a tunable number of procedurally generated follow-up change requests
r: Include: new multi-turn benchmark where agents build and extend an application from a spec, comparing six harnesses and seven models, so evaluation method and project level both hold.

q: ICAE-Bench, an interactive benchmark evaluating how effectively coding agents build repositories from ambiguous product requirements
sec: VI. Conclusion and Future Work, p. 9
r: Include: benchmark for project-level building from natural-language requirements with a new interactive evaluation protocol.

q: LOOPSBENCH makes loop engineering a measurable dimension of coding agent evaluation alongside end state scoring
r: Include: new long-horizon development benchmark with loop-trace metrics, comparing agents and loop implementations, so the evaluation method is the contribution.

q: SWE-RPG combines 163 real PR-derived tasks, executable patch oracles, and validated Clarification and Plan GTs
r: EC6: SWE-bench-style issue resolution on PR-derived repository tasks, which is always excluded.

q: synthesizes 164 scholarly works, 100 practitioner records, 29 benchmark records, and 17 author-system case records through a structured multivocal review
r: Include: secondary study (multivocal review with a described search) on evaluating and operating coding agents, covering variance, baselines, cost and context mechanisms.

q: GAMEXPERT-BENCH, an execution-grounded benchmark for evaluating coding agents across game generation, diagnosis and repair, and human-guided optimization
r: EC6: benchmark limited to one specialised domain (game development) with domain-specific scoring, not a general evaluation-method contribution.

q: 20 long-horizon whole-repository migrations drawn from real open-source infrastructure
r: Include: whole-repository, project-level code change with a new three-stage evaluation protocol (migration audit, tests, agentic verification) over 520 scored runs; the method is the contribution.

q: DeltaSelect turns the repeated trials into a fixed, budget-constrained task set
r: Include: main contribution is an evaluation method for comparing coding-agent configurations with run-to-run variance and dollar cost under control (EC6 ii).

q: We introduce GameLogicBench, a benchmark of 72 gameplay-logic tasks in Godot projects
r: EC6: benchmark limited to one specialised domain (Godot game logic) with domain-specific tick-level assertions.
